title: Controls behind glass, fog and refracted light
blurb: Four more controls from ui-feed.dev: a password field under condensation that you wipe with a finger, a <select> under a lens that refracts the drawn room behind it, a range that splits a beam through a prism, and a colour picker whose foil is thin-film interference. The shared WebGL context shades a drawImage() copy of the canvas, so no pixels are read back.
question: Can a control be put behind a piece of glass computed by a fragment shader, and under fog that is wiped away, and still be typed into and dragged?
result: Yes in the test browser. The control draws its elements, copies that rectangle to a plain canvas with drawImage(), and one shared WebGL context shades the copy. The fog needs only ctx.filter and destination-out.
